config.title: Micro-frontend Shell

intro.title: Micro-frontend Shell
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a micro-frontend shell application using Angular. This shell will act as a main container that dynamically loads and displays different micro-frontend applications. You'll learn the core concept of lazy loading modules to integrate these separate applications. The main technologies involved are Angular modules, components, and the Angular Router. By the end, you'll have a foundational shell that can host multiple micro-frontends.
intro.usecase: A micro-frontend shell is the foundational container application used in large-scale platforms like e-commerce sites or enterprise dashboards. For example, a corporate portal's main layout—containing a global header, navigation sidebar, and user profile panel—acts as the shell that dynamically loads independent micro-apps for different departments (sales, HR, analytics). This pattern allows separate teams to develop, test, and deploy features like product catalogs or reporting modules independently, without disrupting the entire application. As a developer, you'll implement this shell to orchestrate these modular UIs, ensuring a cohesive user experience while enabling scalable, team-aligned development.

objectives: Construct a shell application using Angular CLI to serve as the host for micro-frontends
Configure the shell's routing module to define navigation paths for different micro-frontends
Implement a dynamic component loader to render micro-frontends within the shell application
Integrate communication mechanisms between the shell and loaded micro-frontends
Apply lazy loading techniques to optimize the shell's performance when loading micro-frontends
Initialize and control the lifecycle of micro-frontends from within the shell application
Bind shared dependencies and services between the shell and micro-frontend modules

steps.title: Import Angular core modules and Router
steps.instruction: Import Component and NgModule from '@angular/core', and RouterModule and Routes from '@angular/router'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with the correct module paths. Separate multiple imports with commas.
steps.seedCode: // Import the required Angular modules here
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Angular core and router modules are imported for building the shell application.
successCriteria: Component and NgModule are imported from '@angular/core', and RouterModule and Routes are imported from '@angular/router'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some modules, but check if you have all required imports: Component, NgModule from '@angular/core', and RouterModule, Routes from '@angular/router'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Make sure to import Component and NgModule from '@angular/core', and RouterModule and Routes from '@angular/router'.

steps.title: Create the main AppComponent shell
steps.instruction: Create the AppComponent class with the @Component decorator. Define its selector as 'app-root' and provide a basic template with a heading that says 'Micro-frontend Shell'.
steps.hint: In Angular, a component is a TypeScript class decorated with @Component. The selector is used in HTML, and the template defines the view.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component } from '@angular/core';

// Create the AppComponent class here
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class is defined with the correct decorator, selector, and a simple template.
successCriteria: AppComponent class exists with @Component decorator, selector 'app-root', and template containing 'Micro-frontend Shell'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have all required parts: the @Component decorator with selector 'app-root' and a template with the heading.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AppComponent shell isn't set up correctly. Check that you have a class with @Component decorator, selector 'app-root', and a template.

steps.title: Define the application routes
steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, create a routes array with path and component properties for different micro-frontends. Use the Route interface from '@angular/router'.
steps.hint: Define an array of route objects where each object has a 'path' property (string) and a 'component' property (component class). You can use placeholder components for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent will have a routes array defined with at least one route object containing path and component properties.
successCriteria: A routes array is defined inside the AppComponent class with proper Route type annotation and at least one route object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your routes array is properly typed and contains at least one complete route object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The routes array is missing or incomplete. Remember to define an array of Route objects with path and component properties.

steps.title: Set up the AppModule with routing
steps.instruction: Create the AppModule class with the @NgModule decorator that imports RouterModule.forRoot() and declares AppComponent.
steps.hint: Define a class named AppModule and use the @NgModule decorator with imports and declarations arrays.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppModule is defined with routing configuration and AppComponent declared.
successCriteria: AppModule class exists with @NgModule decorator containing RouterModule.forRoot() in imports and AppComponent in declarations.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have both RouterModule.forRoot() in imports and AppComponent in declarations.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AppModule setup is incomplete. Check that you're using @NgModule with proper imports and declarations.

steps.title: Add navigation links to the template
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent template, add a navigation bar with two anchor tags using routerLink directives to navigate between the 'home' and 'dashboard' routes.
steps.hint: Use the routerLink directive with the route paths you defined earlier. The navigation bar should be placed inside the template property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent template will have a navigation bar with links to the home and dashboard routes using routerLink.
successCriteria: The template contains a <nav> element with two <a> tags that have routerLink directives set to '/home' and '/dashboard'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some navigation elements, but ensure both routerLink directives are present and correctly point to '/home' and '/dashboard'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The navigation links are missing or incorrect. Check that you've added a <nav> with two <a> tags using routerLink.

steps.title: Add router outlet for content display
steps.instruction: Add a <router-outlet> element inside the AppComponent template to serve as the placeholder where routed micro-frontend components will be rendered.
steps.hint: The router-outlet is a special Angular directive that acts as a dynamic insertion point for components based on the current route.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent template now contains a <router-outlet> element, enabling Angular Router to render the appropriate micro-frontend component when a navigation link is clicked.
successCriteria: The AppComponent template includes a <router-outlet> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the <router-outlet> element inside the template property of the @Component decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The router outlet element is missing. Add <router-outlet></router-outlet> to the AppComponent template to create a placeholder for routed components.

steps.title: Create placeholder micro-frontend components
steps.instruction: Create a simple HomeComponent with a template that displays 'Home Micro-frontend' inside a div.
steps.hint: Add a new component class with a template property. Use the @Component decorator and export the class.
steps.expectedOutcome: A HomeComponent class is created with a basic template showing placeholder content for the home micro-frontend.
successCriteria: HomeComponent is defined with @Component decorator, selector 'app-home', and template containing 'Home Micro-frontend'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component has a template property with the required text and is properly exported.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't quite right. Check that you've used @Component decorator with selector and template properties.

steps.title: Update routes with placeholder components
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent class, update the routes array to include route objects that map each path to its corresponding placeholder component.
steps.hint: Each route object should have a 'path' property and a 'component' property. Use the component names you created earlier (HomeComponent, etc.).
steps.expectedOutcome: The routes array will contain route objects that connect each path to its corresponding placeholder component.
successCriteria: The routes array is defined with at least one route object containing both 'path' and 'component' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure each route object has both a 'path' and 'component' property. Check that you're using the correct component names.
steps.feedbackWrong: The routes array needs to be properly configured. Each route should map a path to a component. Review the route configuration syntax.

steps.title: Add basic styling to the shell
steps.instruction: Add a styles array to the AppComponent decorator with a CSS string that styles the navigation and layout.
steps.hint: In the @Component decorator, add a styles property with an array containing your CSS. You can style the navigation links and layout container.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent will have a styles property in its decorator with CSS that styles the shell navigation and layout.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator includes a styles array with at least one CSS rule for navigation or layout styling.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a styles property, but make sure it contains valid CSS rules for navigation or layout.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AppComponent decorator should include a styles array with CSS for styling the shell.

steps.title: Test the micro-frontend shell navigation
steps.instruction: Run the application and click the navigation links to verify routing works between the placeholder components.
steps.hint: Use the Angular CLI command 'ng serve' to start the development server, then open your browser to the provided localhost URL and test the navigation.
steps.expectedOutcome: The application runs successfully and you can navigate between the placeholder micro-frontend components using the navigation links.
successCriteria: Application starts without errors and navigation between routes works correctly.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: The application runs but navigation might not be fully functional. Check that all routes are properly configured and the router outlet is correctly placed in the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The application fails to run or navigation doesn't work. Verify your Angular setup, route configurations, and that all necessary components are properly declared.
